title: Averaging for the probabilistic method
statement: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type and $\beta$ a finite nonempty type, let $\mathrm{Bad} \subseteq \alpha$ be a finite set, let $\mathrm{Fail} \subseteq \alpha \times \beta$ be a decidable relation, and let $C$ be a natural number. Suppose that for every $a \in \mathrm{Bad}$ we have $\abs{\{b \in \beta : \mathrm{Fail}(a,b)\}} \cdot C \le \abs{\beta}$. Then there exists a single $b \in \beta$ such that $\abs{\{a \in \mathrm{Bad} : \mathrm{Fail}(a,b)\}} \cdot C \le \abs{\mathrm{Bad}}$.
